plan: OpenVibe.Vision v1 (plan 2026-10-28 §5.8): ask a picture, compare models side by side, OCR with a local engine first, and the UI check as an API other services call; §5.8b adds faces with separate purpose-scoped consent; wave 1 adds the six network tools
runtime: node 22, express 4, PostgreSQL 18 (openvibe-sdk/db, async) + Valkey 9, Tesseract 5, sharp, onnxruntime-node (YuNet/SFace), Transformers.js (CLIP/DETR)
summary: OpenVibe.Vision reads images and checks UI faults, and its network tools produce alt text, owner-scoped private image search, receipt lines, product matches, camera detections and moments. Local face detection and blur use no identity; personal matching requires separately signed, purpose-scoped consent. General answers keep no image bytes. Opt-in face uploads and templates are encrypted, private and deletable. AI text never describes a person's looks.
works: Ask a picture: multipart upload, data URL or public image URL; task ask/describe/identify/count/translate/ocr; auto/local/ai modes
Local-first OCR: Tesseract 5 on this host, word boxes and mean confidence, zero cost, an optional AI fallback only after an empty local pass
OpenVibe.AI gateway: first-party service token (ai.run.create, namespace ai.*), OpenAI-compatible image message, AI provenance, quota and cost, no direct provider
Compare: local OCR plus one AI run per model hint, requested vs answered model, measured latency and AI cost, sample rows
UI check: static HTML/CSS pass (overflow, cut-off, contrast, overlap, layering), public URL pass with SSRF guard, screenshot pass through OCR boxes and sharp pixels
No looks: public AI text is passed through noLooks; an answer that names looks is replaced by a neutral sentence
Local face detection and blur through YuNet without templates or tracking; detect/blur are open and rate-limited
Consent-scoped SFace matching: verify (1:1), self search in own Vision uploads, adult cast rosters and region-gated private library grouping
Encrypted face templates, opt-in uploads and vectors (AES-256-GCM); immediate template/tag erasure on opt-out and a daily three-year retention job
Network tools: routed alt text, owner-scoped CLIP index/find, Tesseract-first receipts, product vectors, DETR watch and moments, each with a receipt
MCP on /mcp with RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, token challenges and route-equivalent capability checks
vision.result.ready and vision.alert published through OpenVibe.Events when configured, through a durable outbox: a failed publish waits in event_outbox and is retried with backoff
Answers, compare samples, private index and UI checks stored without image bytes; account export/deletion over every table including faces and the private index
Network sign-in as OAuth client vision (PKCE S256, vision_at/vision_rt/vision_oauth), truthful readiness, loopback metrics
Server-rendered pages with stable vi- ids/classes, discovery artifacts, deploy unit and nginx vhost, CI
notYet: Public Vision Arena leaderboards and public test sets (v2); v1 stores aggregate compare samples and exposes them without subjects
OpenCV jobs placed on OpenVibe.Run; v1 uses Tesseract on this host and sharp for pixels
A real browser-rendered UI pass (JavaScript execution, getBoundingClientRect, computed styles); v1 is a documented static pass plus a screenshot pass
Search documents/outbox: v1 has no public records to index
A per-person history page; saved answers are reachable by id for their owner and staff
A tested liveness / presentation-attack detector: verify and cast enrolment return liveness "not_checked"
Media-object search through a source-owner grant: find yourself currently searches only the person's Vision uploads
The capability manifests and grants; the main session registers vision.* and grants them
features: model compare with cost and latency
UI check: overflow, cut-off, contrast, overlap, layering
network tools: alt, index/find, receipt, product, watch, moments
deployment: not deployed: the unit and nginx vhost are deploy/systemd/openvibe-vision.service and deploy/nginx/openvibe.vision.conf
